result.title: A Generative Foundation Model for Multimodal Tokamak Tasks
result.summary: Tokamak experiments record diverse measurements, including waveforms, profiles, fields, and scalars, which are used to reconstruct the plasma, forecast its evolution, recover associated control signals, and estimate disruption risk. Most models are built separately for one task and a fixed set of inputs and outputs, and each relies on a prescribed subset of diagnostics rather than structuring the full multimodal observation set to extract global, cross-signal information about the discharge. These limitations motivate a reusable foundation model that adapts to each task's input-output schema and models heterogeneous target signals jointly, rather than retraining a separate model for every configuration. In this work, we extend the TokaMark benchmark with two groups of tasks for actuator action inversion and disruption prediction, yielding 20 MAST tasks in six groups with explicit schemas and evaluation protocols. Then, we introduce GenToka, a generative tokamak foundation model that jointly generates schema-selected targets through a shared conditional diffusion Transformer, with signal-specific codecs preserving native time series, profiles, fields, and scalars; foundation pretraining and task-specific adaptation transfer cross-signal structure across all six groups. Evaluation on MAST measurements shows that GenToka reduces macro-average normalized root mean squared error relative to TokaMind by 4.7% on Groups 1-4 and by 17.7% on Group 5, and improves macro-average window-level F1 on Group 6 by 8.4% at a common validation-selected threshold. GenToka provides a reusable, generative, and multimodal pathway for experimental tokamaks, linking plasma-state reconstruction, actuator inference, and disruption warning from shared measurements to support more integrated, data-driven fusion plasma prediction and control research.

AI.brief_summary: 论文扩展 TokaMark 基准到 20 个 MAST 托卡马克任务，并提出 GenToka：用共享条件扩散 Transformer 配合各信号专用编解码器，按 schema 联合生成波形、剖面、场与标量等异质目标，实现跨任务预训练与适配。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「schema 条件选择＋模态专用 codec＋共享扩散生成」的结构，可能为 LVR 中异质多模态证据的条件生成、状态解码与跨任务复用提供可核查线索，但论文面向聚变诊断，未涉及视觉推理或 latent 状态分析。
